identity.title: Bind MCP server ownership and cancellation settlement to existing lifecycle owners

closure_unit.outcome: MCP server children and requests retain exact ownership through startup, cancellation, reconnect, crash and caller destruction, using existing ProcessOwnershipLedger and SandboxAdapter contracts; stopped/settled is reported only after authoritative observation.

materialized_acceptance.text: Route each new MCP stdio server through the existing approved SandboxAdapter attached-process/stdio contract and ProcessOwnershipLedger ownership path. Preserve CREATE_NO_WINDOW and quiet operation. Bind process_uuid, actual PID generation/executable identity, owner runtime instance, ModelSession, account/resource scope and adapter identity before exposing the child as usable; a bare PID is insufficient.

If spawn succeeds but pipe setup, ownership registration, START durability, dispatcher setup or reconnect adoption fails, retain the exact child cleanup owner or perform bounded authorized compensation. Preserve truthful open/cleanup-failed state on unresolved cleanup; no returned error may silently abandon a created child.

Reuse WP-1 MT-019 running-app reclaim, restart reconcile, exact-owner fencing and periodic recovery, plus WP-KERNEL-012 MT-137 SurrealDB durability. Consume these APIs from mcp. Do not implement a second scanner/reaper, kill by executable name, create private process state, weaken an identity fence or independently rewrite their contracts.

McpCall drop, timeout or user cancellation records cancellation requested and sends protocol-valid notifications/cancelled through MT-204's reserved control capacity. Successful notification delivery, dropping the future and request-map removal do not prove the server stopped work. A cooperative server needs observable request settlement; an ignored or unobservable cancellation remains unknown or cancellation pending under the existing typed status contract.

Terminate a child only through its actual owning adapter and scoped recovery policy when the entire owned session/process may be retired. A single cancelled request on a shared healthy MCP server must not kill that server or interrupt other clients. External/shared/unowned servers remain externally owned; absent request-settlement evidence is explicit uncertainty, never a kill permission.

Reconnect cannot replace an owned server merely after start_kill. Observe old child exit and reap, settle or durably transfer required ownership, and reconcile old-generation requests before releasing its ownership capacity and adopting another generation. Retain partial results and unknown side-effect outcomes; do not replay non-idempotent work blindly.

STOP/stopped_at and released process/reclamation permits require authoritative observed termination/settlement, never cancellation intent, send success, task abort or start_kill success. Failed/timeout kill or reap retains an open durable row and visible typed cleanup failure. Repeated stop, callback and restart replay is idempotent; delayed START cannot erase STOP and an old generation cannot stop a new child.

Real owned-server proof covers cooperative cancellation, ignored cancellation, child crash, owned descendants, broken pipes/reconnect, caller destruction and application restart. Compare OS/adapter process identity and exit/reap state with canonical SurrealDB rows across reopen. Verify owned descendants retire under the existing containment contract while unrelated and shared clients remain running.

Default deny applies to spawn, cancellation, settlement lookup, recovery and diagnostic inspection. Prove wrong account, same-project private resource, wrong process generation, wrong runtime instance, stale/revoked grant and switched context cannot inspect or affect another request/server. Recovery uses original immutable ownership; it cannot relabel a process to the current UI account.

Flight Recorder retains scoped business events for launch, cancellation request, observed completion/stop and unknown/failure outcomes through existing schemas. internal_diagnostics records typed lifecycle, outstanding-settlement, cleanup/ownership failure and timeout health metadata. Existing standalone Palmistry passively records child liveness/stall/crash/survivor state across host failure; observed quietness is not request completion.

Provide the typed backend request/process/settlement state/schema and same-change UserManual interface for MT-209 through Primary. The contract distinguishes requested cancellation, local timeout, unknown remote outcome, observed stop and cleanup failure. Backend acceptance proves those states and backend diagnostic outputs independently. MT-209 owns Dev Command Center/Argus presentation and end-to-end GUI proof required for WP closure; completed MT-209 acceptance is not a prerequisite for this backend MT PASS.

Identify the real production MCP caller and run independently admitted acceptance through that caller with the owning adapter, existing managed SurrealDB and the existing diagnostic tiers. Schema, persistence-owner, shared API, manual and publication changes stay with Primary and their existing module contracts. Missing integration or owning proof blocks acceptance; this MT creates no run allowance or parent-WP PASS.

ownership.team_policy: One current Coding, Codecheck and Diagnostics trio assigned by Codeleader. Creating this MT does not activate another team, release a source lease or grant a compiler/runtime slot.
ownership.shared_write_policy: Primary owns shared publication, source integration, manifest/schema and UserManual writes. Submit exact typed changes through the existing allocation; do not edit those paths from this MT.

execution.boundary_change: Extend the existing mcp request/transport owner and its typed clients. Preserve dependency direction; do not create a second scheduler, reaper, permission authority or diagnostics framework.
execution.build_unit_policy: Use small focused files inside the owning logical mcp module and independently select its affected dependency/test closure. No forced crate split, aggregate sink crate or invented build cap. Apply crate build-budget accounting only where the actual project contract makes it applicable.
execution.module_lifecycle_policy: Preserve this in-flight WP's original governance/source/spec pins. Reuse existing public ownership APIs. A verified missing reusable asset capability requires a separate canonical-source MT and independently verified immutable publication before a distinct host-adoption MT; this planned contract does not invent a repository or authorize publication.

conditional_dependencies.when: Reuse exact-scope reclaim/restart/fencing and its valid proof. Any open owning defect or changed dependency requires that owner to resolve it; this MT grants no edits there.
Preserve current SurrealDB process-ledger durability and reopen proof; schema/persistence changes remain with Primary.
Consume the existing bounded operation-watchdog contract; no duplicated watchdog.
Consume existing child registration and Palmistry survivor proof; no watcher authority expansion.
MCP drain joins production shutdown. The exact production main consumer and settlement failure reporting remain owned by Primary under the existing held contract.

shared_integration_dependencies.requirement: Read-only integration references. Primary and the existing owning module contracts handle any necessary shared API, schema, production adoption, shutdown and manual publication; no write authority transfers to this MCP MT.

MT-209 consumes this backend MT published state/schema/manual interface and owns native Dev Command Center, Argus and end-to-end GUI proof for WP closure. This backend MT owns backend diagnostics proof and can pass independently of completed MT-209 acceptance.

checks.expected: MCP has one process cleanup owner; cancel/send/start_kill cannot produce a STOP or release unsettled process permits. Shared-server requests retain isolation.
checks.timeout_policy: Resolve the owning checked-in per-test timeout and exact selector at admission. No whole-round wall-clock wrapper; missing timeout/selector blocks that run.
evidence_required: Exact owner/adapter/ledger call graph and candidate inputs
Primary-owned shared API/schema changes or explicit absence
Current WP-1 MT-019 and MT-137 dependency proof references

Use only owned test children; exercise cooperative/ignored cancellation, crash, descendants, broken pipes, reconnect, caller destruction and failed spawn/registration. Reuse existing process_ledger_surreal_tests, process_runtime_owner_identity_surreal_tests and process_reclaim_real_lifecycle_surreal_tests where their inputs remain valid; owning module changes receive owning proof, not copies here.
checks.expected: Observed OS/adapter identity and exit/reap match canonical ledger state. Unknown cancellation stays unknown, failed cleanup remains open, old-generation server cannot be replaced without settlement, and shared/unrelated processes are unaffected.
checks.timeout_policy: Resolve the owning checked-in per-test timeout and exact selector at admission. No whole-round wall-clock wrapper; missing timeout/selector blocks that run.
evidence_required: Real process identities, ownership scope, exit/reap observations and canonical SurrealDB reread
Cooperative versus ignored-cancel results distinguish request and server lifetime
Owned descendants cleaned through existing containment
Per-case bounded wait result and nonzero test counts

Exercise wrong generation/runtime/account, revoked grant, duplicate STOP and late START; prove the backend state/schema/manual interface consumed by MT-209 without requiring its completed GUI acceptance.
checks.expected: Only exact owned stale children are eligible for reclaim. Terminal and unresolved rows remain truthful across reopen and duplicate events; no unrelated owner or private metadata is exposed.

evidence_required: Canonical before/after rows and actual process observation
Valid reuse references or fresh owning restart proof
Exact-resource denial and scoped positive cases
No-context UserManual recovery and published backend request/process/settlement state/schema interface

checks.command_or_method: Use existing tier consumers during the real owned child lifecycle and separately admitted host-failure case. Reconcile Flight Recorder business events, internal health reports and surviving standalone Palmistry records with the same opaque correlation.
checks.expected: Observed cancel-request, unknown, failure and stopped states agree with process/ledger evidence. Palmistry survives to observe; it neither kills nor restarts. Tier-specific output contains no project data.
checks.timeout_policy: Resolve the owning checked-in per-test timeout and exact selector at admission. No whole-round wall-clock wrapper; missing timeout/selector blocks that run.
evidence_required: Flight Recorder business history and replay with scoped lookup
Real Palmistry retained child-stall/crash/survivor record and no-false-positive case
Typed backend allowlist/privacy review and diagnostic projection/schema evidence; MT-209 Argus proof remains a separate WP closure requirement

proof.execution_authority: No runtime/build/test/fetch grant is created. Codecheck and Diagnostics are the current independent partners assigned by Codeleader; no implementer self-verdict.
proof.evidence_policy: Bind exact commit/tree, relevant input paths, entrypoint/config, actual managed resources and per-check artifacts. Reuse unchanged proof only with empty input intersection. Missing caller, process settlement or tier evidence cannot be replaced by mocks, status text, screenshots alone or declaration.
proof.artifact_policy: Resolve the sole Codex artifact root from the live kernel or existing authorized environment, and use the owning WP/MT allocation. Reuse the WP compiler target under physical custody; no per-MT compiler cache or new root.
proof.required_scope: Focused module cases precede affected production boundary and independent acceptance. Preserve original WP/CKC/WP-1 held proofs and runtime restrictions.
proof.backend_acceptance_boundary: The backend MT owns its actual production caller, typed state/schema/manual interface and three-tier backend diagnostics evidence. Completed MT-209 GUI/Argus acceptance is not a backend PASS prerequisite; it remains independently mandatory for WP closure.

Owned server/process references and business-event projections

identity_and_scope_contexts: Authenticated account, acting and owning Principal, AccessSpace, ModelSession, project/workspace, resource and delegation context
Existing capability intersection, authorization receipt, correlation and revocation epoch
enforcement_boundaries: Admission, actual dispatch, retry/reconnect, response delivery, cancellation, settlement lookup and diagnostic projection
same_project_private_resource_cases: Two accounts in one project cannot discover or cancel each other's private request/process; an explicitly granted shared resource remains usable.
cross_account_negative_cases: An unrelated account and missing, invalid, stale, revoked, mismatched or ambiguous context cannot admit, inspect, cancel or recover another request.
derived_resource_non_widening_cases: Results, error receipts, replay and diagnostic projections retain source scope; late completions cannot widen it.
revocation_and_context_switch_cases: Queued/reconnecting work rechecks current grants before dispatch and rejects revoked work.
A context switch never retargets an accepted request; immutable original identity remains bound through settlement.
remote_saas_mcp_sync_cases: Reconnect preserves server identity, request id, correlation, resource scope and audience-bound delegation; a changed server/grant cannot inherit old authority.
metadata_side_channel_cases: No command, arguments, prompts, tool payloads, tokens, file names or restricted existence metadata enter internal_diagnostics or Palmistry.
Flight Recorder and manual/status lookup enforce scope and retain existing redaction rules.
expected_evidence: Revocation during queue/reconnect and late-response case
No foreign-request cancellation or process disruption

handoff.coordination: Use the current Codeleader allocation and Primary physical custody. No outgoing external chat, role launch or new team is authorized by this record.

risks: Cancel notification or start_kill is misreported as stopped while work remains live.
Reconnecting replaces a child before exit/reap and loses process ownership or permits.
One request cancellation kills a shared server or unrelated PID generation.
Failed START/registration/pipe setup leaves an unowned child; durable failure becomes a fabricated STOP.
A new reaper or hidden store diverges from existing exact-owner reclaim and restart rules.
minimum_controls: Separate local completion, cancellation requested, unknown remote outcome and observed settlement.
Retain the actual cleanup owner and process identity until authoritative termination/reap and durable settlement.
Use existing adapter containment, exact generation/runtime/resource fencing and shared-client negative proof.
Failed cleanup remains open, observable and recoverable through the existing owner.
Reuse WP-1 MT-019, MT-137 and MT-105/106; Primary owns shared changes and original acceptance remains independent.

operator_authority.preservation: Original three-WP scope, source/spec/governance pins, held cases, historical verdicts, independent acceptance and spent run history remain unchanged.

anchors.meaning: Pending request tracking, timeout and notifications/cancelled. Sending the notification is a cancellation request; the claim that it ensures remote CPU work stops requires separately observed settlement.
Current scoped authority, aggregate admission including waiting producers and reclamation, reserved completion/cancellation service, actual retirement and failed-spawn ownership.
Preserve canonical tool identity, schemas, side effects, idempotency, capability intersection, ModelSession correlation, payload sizing and typed error behavior.
Every Handshake-spawned process uses ProcessOwnershipLedger and the existing SandboxAdapter reclaim owner; terminal rows require observed outcomes.

spec_basis.pin_policy: These anchors explain the approved additive work; reading the current bundle does not re-pin original acceptance or rewrite existing MTs.

inspection.source_state: Inspected source only; no runtime, build, test or deployment result created.

source_evidence.finding: Reconnect requests start_kill without observed wait/reap. Direct spawn already uses kill_on_drop and CREATE_NO_WINDOW; preserve these existing safeguards.
Drop removes request metadata and sends notifications/cancelled; it observes no remote settlement.
The timeout test proves cancellation notification receipt only.
Existing attached ownership, cleanup and restart APIs are the integration boundary.
Existing decorator/attached paths require exact ownership and observed-settlement inspection before adoption. API presence alone does not prove this MCP path is ledger-bound.
Existing reclaim outcomes distinguish failure and pending durable STOP; reuse the owner instead of creating a new reaper.

context_capsule.caller_evidence: Search found GatedMcpClient constructors in MCP/model-session tests and the internal JsonRpc client construction in mcp/gate.rs. No shipped production MCP constructor caller was verified. Establish the actual production adoption path before claiming end-to-end product acceptance; do not assert a deployed process explosion.

supplied_document.role: Operator-supplied reliability lessons; non-authoritative research input. Only evaluated lessons bound here become task requirements.

official_sources.basis: Parent's inspected official MCP cancellation research; cancellation can race with completion and recipients may be unable to cancel. Preserve request-id and initialization constraints.
Parent's inspected Tokio channel research; bound queues and producer admission rather than moving the unbounded allocation upstream.
Parent's inspected Tokio process research; a kill request and process exit/reap are distinct observations.

research_basis.selected_approach: Extend current typed MCP state and consume existing host owners. Preserve the server contract, privacy and correlation while bounding accepted work and reporting uncertain outcomes.
rejected_options: Treat cancellation notification, dropped future or kill request as remote work settlement.
Add a second reaper/watchdog/permission store or use a static fixture as product adoption proof.
Copy external sample implementations or unverified proposed limits into product authority.

diagnostic_result_policy: Record future per-tier WIRED only after its required observed output is inspected. NOT_APPLICABLE needs a concrete reason; DEFERRED names the unresolved owner/dependency and does not satisfy a required acceptance row. This planned record asserts none of those future outcomes.
